issue_families.name: Connector authorization expired or revoked
issue_families.summary: OAuth grants or stored credentials used by an inbound connector are revoked, expire, rotate or lose scope (authorizing user deactivated, password rotation, short token lifetimes), so syncs fail or quietly return nothing.
issue_families.boundary_note: The credential is the connector's access to the source system, not a person signing in to our app (auth) or a client calling our public API (api).

issue_families.name: Stuck or hung sync jobs
issue_families.summary: Runs that never finish: orphaned job locks, crashed workers with no heartbeat, endless loops on bad source data, source requests without timeouts, or two jobs deadlocking.
issue_families.boundary_note: The stuck work is ingestion from a source; general application slowness under load would be perf.

issue_families.name: Duplicate records from ingestion
issue_families.summary: Records inserted twice because source IDs change on merge or re-import, ingestion paths use different keys, overlapping windows lack a unique key, or file uploads append instead of replace.
issue_families.boundary_note: The duplicates are created by ingestion itself, so sync rather than data_quality, which covers wrong calculations on correctly ingested data.

issue_families.name: Incremental cursor gaps
issue_families.summary: Incremental syncs skip records because the source does not update modification timestamps, records arrive late or backdated, or the cursor mishandles local time.
issue_families.boundary_note: The records are never ingested, which stays sync even when time zones are involved; mis-bucketing of ingested data would be data_quality.

issue_families.name: Pagination and truncated pulls
issue_families.summary: Source offset caps, expiring page tokens, truncated nested records, unstable sort orders and page-count safeguards make a sync stop early while reporting success.
issue_families.boundary_note: Data is missing because the pull from the source was incomplete; this is ingestion, not a fault in our own public API (api).

issue_families.name: Source schema changes
issue_families.summary: Renamed, deleted or retyped source fields, retired source API versions and new picklist values break field mappings, fail runs or blank values.
issue_families.boundary_note: The value never arrives because the mapping broke during ingestion, so sync rather than data_quality.

issue_families.name: File-based ingestion (CSV uploads and SFTP drops)
issue_families.summary: Encoding, delimiter and decimal conventions, file-name patterns and partially written files cause rejected, garbled or incomplete imports of customer-supplied files.
issue_families.boundary_note: These are inbound files being ingested; CSV or Excel files produced by our app are export.

issue_families.name: Source API quotas and throttling
issue_families.summary: Customer-side API allowances or source rate limits are exhausted by other tools, peak traffic or backfills, so runs stop, lag or are skipped.
issue_families.boundary_note: The limits are imposed by the source on our connector, not our public API rate limits (api); the delay is in ingestion rather than app performance (perf).

issue_families.name: Deletions, cancellations and edits not propagated
issue_families.summary: Hard deletes, cancellations, standalone refunds, archived items and post-fulfilment adjustments are never fetched, leaving stale records in dashboards.
issue_families.boundary_note: Totals look wrong because state changes were never ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.

issue_families.name: Sync scheduling and auto-pause
issue_families.summary: Schedules auto-paused after failures with notices sent to inactive recipients, schedules in the wrong time zone, frequency lost after a plan change, and runs skipped at daylight-saving transitions.
issue_families.boundary_note: This is about when ingestion runs: not alert rules (alerts), not workspace time-zone preferences (workspace_admin), and no charge is wrong (billing).

issue_families.name: Connector access scope in the source system
issue_families.summary: Integration users or app installs lack read access to regions, objects, fields or scopes in the source, so part of the data arrives and part does not.
issue_families.boundary_note: The permissions live in the customer's source system and govern what the connector can read; roles inside our app are perm.

issue_families.name: Source account, store and instance selection
issue_families.summary: The connector points at the wrong instance (sandbox or decommissioned) or omits new stores, storefronts or advertising accounts.
issue_families.boundary_note: Data never ingested from the right source account is sync, not a reporting or permission issue.

issue_families.name: Initial historical backfill
issue_families.summary: First loads with a short default history, run-duration caps, non-resumable retries, mismatched object coverage, or backfills that block daily syncs.
issue_families.boundary_note: Concerns the initial ingestion of history, so sync; app-wide slowness on large datasets is perf.

issue_families.name: Inbound event (webhook) ingestion
issue_families.summary: Real-time events from source platforms are rejected after signing-secret rotation, lost when subscriptions disappear or intake overflows, or never registered for added stores; data then arrives only with the scheduled catch-up sync.
issue_families.boundary_note: These are inbound events used to ingest source data, so sync; our outbound webhooks and public API belong to api.

related_groups.shared_root_cause: The user who authorized the connector was deactivated or removed in the source system, which revoked the OAuth grant the connector depended on.
The source system assigns new record IDs when records are merged or re-imported, so upserting by external ID inserts them as new rows.
The source changes records through bulk or import tools without updating their last-modified timestamp, so the incremental sync skips them.
A custom field was renamed or recreated in the source, leaving the connector's field mapping pointing at a name that no longer exists.
Files saved on computers with European regional settings use semicolon separators and decimal commas, which the importer parsed with default assumptions.
Other applications consume the customer CRM's shared daily API allowance, so the connector runs out of quota partway through a run.
The connection auto-paused after consecutive failures and its failure notifications went to an inactive user, so nobody noticed.
The event signing secret was rotated in the commerce platform but not in the connector, so every inbound event was rejected and only the scheduled sync delivered data.
A cancelled run left its job lock in place, so later runs waited on it or refused to start.

tickets.subject: CRM connector stopped syncing after an admin left
tickets.description: Customer reports opportunity data in the pipeline dashboard has not changed since last Thursday. The connector page shows 'Authorization invalid'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The CRM connection had been authorized by an admin who has since left the company, and deactivating their CRM user revoked the refresh token. The customer re-authorized the connector with a dedicated integration user in their CRM. A manual sync completed and pulled in four days of opportunity changes.

tickets.classification_rationale: Triggered by staff offboarding, but the impact is an inbound connector that stopped ingesting, so sync rather than perm.
tickets.subject: Order sync failing with 'invalid_grant' since staff offboarding
tickets.description: The Northwind Commerce connector log shows 'invalid_grant: refresh token revoked' on every run since Monday, the day the customer offboarded several staff.
tickets.resolution_notes: One of the removed staff accounts was the store-owner login used to authorize the connection, and removing it invalidated the grant. The customer reconnected with a service account not tied to an individual, and the connector page now shows which user authorized the connection. Sync resumed and backfilled the 2,310 orders from the gap.

tickets.subject: Loyalty figures frozen after connector owner changed roles
tickets.description: Loyalty points and member counts stopped updating. The agent found the connection was owned by a marketing manager whose loyalty-platform login was disabled when they moved to another department.
tickets.resolution_notes: Disabling the manager's login on the loyalty platform revoked the token our connector used. The customer re-authorized under a shared integration login with read-only scope. The next scheduled sync completed and member counts matched the platform's own report.

tickets.subject: POS connector needs re-authorizing every 30 days
tickets.description: The customer's point-of-sale connection fails about once a month with 'Credentials expired', and the store operations team has been reconnecting it by hand each time.
tickets.resolution_notes: The POS platform issues access tokens that expire after 30 days, and our connector for that platform never used its refresh flow, so monthly reconnection was the only workaround. Released a connector update that refreshes the token automatically before expiry. The connection has stayed valid through two expiry cycles since.

tickets.classification_rationale: An authentication error appears, but it is the connector's credential to the source ERP, which is sync rather than user sign-in (auth).
tickets.subject: ERP connector fails authentication after password rotation
tickets.description: Right after the customer's ERP admin changed their password as part of a quarterly rotation, the ERP connector began failing with 'Authentication failed (401)'.
tickets.resolution_notes: This ERP connector used basic credentials, so the stored password became invalid after the rotation. The admin updated the stored credentials and, at our suggestion, switched the connection to the ERP's token-based authentication, which does not depend on password rotation. The next sync succeeded and pulled the full day's sales invoices.

tickets.subject: Connector shows 'Connected' but brings in no new data
tickets.description: The connector status page has a green 'Connected' tick, yet no new customer records have arrived for a week.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's CRM admin had reduced the connected app's permissions to profile-only, so token refreshes still succeeded but data requests returned empty results instead of errors. Re-authorized with the full read scope and added a check that flags a connection returning zero records for several consecutive runs. The next run imported 1,180 updated customer records.

tickets.subject: Sync stuck on 'Waiting for previous run' for three nights
tickets.description: Customer's nightly order sync hasn't run for three nights. Each scheduled run shows 'Waiting for previous run to finish', but nothing is actually in progress.
tickets.resolution_notes: A run the customer cancelled midway had not released its job lock, so every later run waited on it. Released the stale lock by hand as a workaround; making cancellation always clear the lock was tracked for a later release. The next scheduled sync completed and caught up all three nights of orders.

tickets.subject: Manual sync refused: 'run already active'
tickets.description: The customer's store analytics lead tries to start a manual sync and gets 'A sync is already running for this connection', although history shows the last run was cancelled yesterday afternoon.
tickets.resolution_notes: Cancelling that run did not release its job lock, so the connection still looked busy. This release makes cancellation release the lock and automatically expires any lock older than the maximum run time. The lock cleared after deployment and the manual sync completed in 14 minutes.

tickets.subject: Product catalog sync hangs at 99%
tickets.description: The product catalog sync progress bar sits at 99% for hours. It finishes after a restart, then hangs again the next day.
tickets.resolution_notes: The final step rebuilds category hierarchies, and a category set as its own parent created a loop the step never left. Added cycle detection that skips and logs the offending record, and the customer corrected the category in their e-commerce admin. The catalog sync has completed in under 20 minutes every day since.

tickets.subject: Inventory sync shows 'Running' after its worker died
tickets.description: The status page showed the inventory sync as 'Running' for 30 hours. No log lines had been written since shortly after it started.
tickets.resolution_notes: The worker handling the run was terminated during a platform node replacement, and with no heartbeat check the run's status was never updated. Added a heartbeat so runs without progress for 15 minutes are marked failed and retried automatically. Restarted the inventory sync, which completed for all 46 store locations.

tickets.classification_rationale: A large data volume is involved, but the job hung waiting on the source rather than running slowly in our app, so sync rather than perf.
tickets.subject: CRM sync stuck on 'Fetching activity history'
tickets.description: For two days the CRM sync has sat on the 'Fetching activity history' step. The customer recently imported ten years of call logs into one key account.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector requested that account's whole activity history in a single call with no timeout, and the source never finished responding. Added request timeouts and changed activity fetching to monthly chunks. The sync completed overnight, including about 410,000 activities for the large account.

tickets.subject: Order and refund syncs block each other
tickets.description: After the customer enabled hourly syncs, the order sync and the refund sync for the same store both sit at 'In progress' and neither finishes.
tickets.resolution_notes: Both jobs wrote to the same order rows, and when the refund job started before the hourly order job finished they waited on each other's row locks. Serialized jobs per connection so the refund sync waits for the order sync. Both jobs have completed every hour since the change.

tickets.classification_rationale: The duplicates show up as wrong counts, but they come from how records were ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Duplicate customer accounts after CRM record merge
tickets.description: The customer's account count in the dashboard jumped by about 300 overnight, and many accounts now appear twice with slightly different names.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's CRM team merged duplicate accounts, and the surviving records received new IDs, so our upsert by external ID inserted them as new rows while the old IDs remained. Processed the CRM's merge events to retire the old IDs and removed 312 orphaned rows. The account count now matches the CRM report.

tickets.subject: Products listed twice after catalog re-import
tickets.description: A sporting goods retailer re-imported their catalog in their e-commerce admin to fix descriptions. The product performance dashboard now lists many items twice, one row holding all historic sales and another holding only recent ones.
tickets.resolution_notes: The re-import gave every product a new platform ID, and the connector keyed products on that ID, so re-imported items looked like new products. Switched the key to SKU for this connection and merged the duplicate pairs so their sales history stays together. Each product now appears once with its complete history.

tickets.subject: Contact totals rose after a CRM dedupe project
tickets.description: The customer's marketing team ran a deduplication project in their CRM, and contact counts in our dashboards went up instead of down.
tickets.resolution_notes: Merging in the CRM gave surviving contacts new IDs, so the connector re-ingested them as new while never receiving deletions for the records that were merged away. Enabled processing of merge and delete events for the connection and ran a cleanup that removed 4,870 stale contacts. Contact totals now match the CRM within the sync interval.

tickets.subject: Orders counted twice from live events and nightly sync
tickets.description: After switching on real-time order events, the customer sees some orders twice in the daily sales chart: once with the event's timestamp and again after the nightly sync.
tickets.resolution_notes: Event-ingested orders were stored with a key prefixed by the store ID, while the scheduled sync used the bare order number, so the nightly run did not recognize them. Normalized both paths to the same order key and deduplicated the affected days. Daily totals matched the store's own order count for the following week.

tickets.subject: March doubled after re-uploading a corrected sales file
tickets.description: Customer uploaded a corrected store-sales CSV for March to replace an earlier file that had errors. The dashboard now shows March at roughly twice its real value.
tickets.resolution_notes: The file upload connection was in append mode, so the corrected file was added on top of the original. Switched the connection to 'replace by date range', removed the earlier upload and reprocessed the corrected file. March totals now match the customer's corrected spreadsheet.

tickets.classification_rationale: Totals were inflated, but by duplicate ingestion from overlapping sync windows, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Refunds inflated after moving to hourly syncs
tickets.description: Refund totals look too high on every day since the customer changed from daily to hourly syncs.
tickets.resolution_notes: The hourly schedule used a two-hour lookback buffer, and refund records had no unique key in the connector mapping, so overlapping windows inserted the same refunds again. Added the refund ID as the unique key so overlapping records update instead of insert, and deduplicated the affected period. Refund totals for those days now match the payments report.

tickets.subject: Bulk status updates in CRM never reach the dashboard
tickets.description: Sales operations closed about 600 stale opportunities with their CRM's bulk update tool, but a week later the pipeline dashboard still shows them as open.
tickets.resolution_notes: The bulk tool changes records without touching their last-modified timestamp, and the connector's incremental sync only fetches records whose timestamp has moved. Ran a full refresh to pick up the changes and enabled the weekly full reconciliation option for this connection. The 600 opportunities now show as closed.

tickets.subject: Stock-take corrections from store app never appear
tickets.description: Stock counts corrected through the e-commerce platform's mobile stock-take app never make it into our inventory dashboards. Edits made in the platform's web admin come through normally.
tickets.resolution_notes: The stock-take app writes adjustments without updating the product's 'updated at' field, so the incremental sync skipped them. Changed this connector to read the platform's inventory-adjustment feed as well as product updates. Corrections from the next store stock-take appeared within one sync cycle.

tickets.subject: Repriced SKUs still show last month's prices
tickets.description: The pricing dashboard still shows old prices for about 2,000 SKUs that the pricing team changed in one spreadsheet import on the 1st.
tickets.resolution_notes: Prices changed through the platform's import tool keep their original modification time, so the incremental sync never saw them. Triggered a full product resync and turned on a nightly full scan of price fields for this connection as a lasting safeguard. Repriced SKUs now show current prices, and the nightly scan also caught the next import.

tickets.classification_rationale: Store network outages are mentioned, but the problem is our ingestion cursor skipping late records, not network reachability, so sync rather than connectivity.
tickets.subject: Late-arriving POS transactions missing for days
tickets.description: Transactions from stores with unreliable internet are missing from the dashboard even days later. Those registers upload their transactions in batches once the connection returns.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector's cursor used the transaction time, and offline registers uploaded transactions timed before the cursor, so they were skipped. Switched the cursor to the POS platform's 'received at' timestamp. The past two weeks of missing transactions were backfilled and new offline batches now appear on the next sync.

tickets.subject: Backdated phone orders never appear
tickets.description: The customer's finance team sometimes enters phone orders with an earlier order date. Those orders never show up in the sales dashboard.
tickets.resolution_notes: Incremental sync filtered on order date rather than creation or modification time, so orders entered later with an earlier date fell behind the cursor. Changed the filter to the order's modification time and reloaded the past 60 days. All 37 backdated orders now appear on their correct dates.

tickets.classification_rationale: Time-related, but the records were never ingested rather than bucketed incorrectly, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Orders from the repeated daylight-saving hour missing
tickets.description: Orders placed during the second 01:00 to 02:00 hour on the night the clocks went back are absent from the dashboard. The source system shows 84 orders in that hour.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector stored its cursor as local time without an offset, so after the first pass through the repeated hour it treated the second pass as already synced. Changed cursors to be stored in UTC and reloaded that night. All 84 orders are now present.

tickets.subject: Only the first 10,000 customers imported
tickets.description: The customer's CRM holds about 38,000 customer records, but our dashboards show exactly 10,000.
tickets.resolution_notes: The CRM's list endpoint stops returning results beyond offset 10,000, and the connector used offset pagination. Switched the connector to cursor-based pagination for that object. A full resync imported all 38,214 records.

tickets.subject: Busiest stores' orders cut off partway through the day
tickets.description: For the two busiest stores, orders in the dashboard stop partway through each day, while smaller stores are complete. Every run reports success.
tickets.resolution_notes: The e-commerce API's page tokens expire after five minutes, and pages for the large stores took longer than that to process, so the next request returned an empty page that the connector read as the end. Changed the connector to fetch all pages before processing and to fail loudly on an expired token. Re-synced both stores, and daily order counts now match the platform.

tickets.subject: Large orders show only their first 50 line items
tickets.description: Order headers are all present, but orders with more than 50 products show only the first 50 in the basket analysis dashboard.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector read line items from the order payload, which the source truncates at 50 items with a 'has more' flag that the connector ignored. Updated the connector to follow the line-item link whenever the flag is set and re-synced the last 90 days of orders. Large wholesale orders now show their full baskets, the largest with 212 lines.

tickets.subject: Different gift cards missing each day
tickets.description: Gift card totals in the dashboard sit about 4% below the e-commerce platform's own report, and a different set of cards is missing every day.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector paged through gift cards sorted by last-used date, so cards used during a sync moved between pages and some were skipped. Changed the request to sort by the immutable card ID. Over the next three days imported gift card counts matched the platform exactly.

tickets.subject: Email-marketing contacts stop at 20,000
tickets.description: The customer's email-marketing connector imports a steady 20,000 contacts out of about 55,000, and each run logs the warning 'Maximum page count reached'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector had a 200-page safety limit set when contact lists were far smaller. Raised the limit for this connector, made it configurable, and changed reaching it into an error rather than a warning. The next sync imported all 55,410 contacts.

tickets.subject: Sync fails: mapped field 'sales_region' not found
tickets.description: The CRM sync has failed on every run since Tuesday with 'Mapped field sales_region does not exist on object Account'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's CRM admin renamed the custom field to sales_territory, and our field mapping still referenced the old API name. Updated the mapping to the new field and backfilled the last week. The sync completed and region filters on the account dashboard show values again.

tickets.classification_rationale: Values looked wrong ('Unknown'), but they were never ingested because the source field changed, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Channel blank for every order since last weekend
tickets.description: Orders synced since last weekend have an empty channel value, so the channel breakdown on the sales dashboard lumps them under 'Unknown'. Older orders are fine.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer replaced the custom order attribute 'sales_channel' with a new one called 'order_channel' in their e-commerce admin, and the connector mapping still pointed at the old attribute, which now returns nothing. Re-mapped to the new attribute and re-synced orders since the change. The channel breakdown shows no 'Unknown' orders for the period.

tickets.subject: Loyalty tier stops updating; warning cites unknown column
tickets.description: Every CRM sync now ends 'Completed with warnings', and customer records no longer update their loyalty tier. The warning text mentions an unknown column.
tickets.resolution_notes: A CRM admin deleted the loyalty_tier field and recreated it with the same label but a different internal name, which broke the existing mapping. Mapped the new internal name and made mapping errors appear on the connector page instead of only as a log warning. Loyalty tiers updated on the next sync for all 12,600 customers.

tickets.subject: Store sync fails after store number became text
tickets.description: Since the customer changed 'store_number' to a text field in their ERP to support codes like 'S-014', the store sync fails with 'Invalid integer value'.
tickets.resolution_notes: Our destination column for store numbers was typed as an integer, so the new alphanumeric values were rejected. Migrated the column to text for this connection and re-ran the sync. All 63 stores imported, including those with the new lettered codes.

tickets.classification_rationale: A third-party API version is involved, but it is our inbound connector failing to ingest, so sync rather than api, which covers our own public API.
tickets.subject: Order sync rejected: source API version no longer supported
tickets.description: Order sync from Northwind Commerce has failed since the start of the month with 'API version 2024-01 is no longer supported'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector was pinned to an API version the platform had announced for retirement, and we had not moved it in time. Upgraded the connector to the current API version, including a renamed discount field, and re-ran the failed days. Orders and discounts for the whole month are now present.

tickets.classification_rationale: Shows up as empty values, but the value was dropped during ingestion, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: New lead source value dropped during sync
tickets.description: The customer added a lead source value 'Pop-up Store' in their CRM. Leads with that source appear in the dashboard with no source at all.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector validated picklist values against a list cached when the connection was created and silently cleared values it didn't recognize. Changed it to refresh picklist definitions on every run and to keep unrecognized values. Re-synced the affected leads, and 'Pop-up Store' now shows 148 leads in the source chart.

tickets.classification_rationale: The text displays garbled, but the characters were corrupted while the file was ingested, so sync rather than render.
tickets.subject: Accented store names garbled after daily file upload
tickets.description: Store names with accents such as 'Café Central' appear as 'CafÃ© Central' after each daily file upload, even though the file looks right in the customer's spreadsheet tool.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's export saved files in Windows-1252 encoding, while the upload connection assumed UTF-8. Added encoding detection to file uploads and set this connection to Windows-1252 explicitly. Reprocessed the last 30 days of files, and all 214 store names now read correctly.

tickets.subject: Daily sales file rejected: 'Expected 9 columns, found 1'
tickets.description: Since a new finance PC was set up at the customer, the daily sales file fails validation with 'Expected 9 columns, found 1'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The new PC uses European regional settings, so the spreadsheet tool saves its CSV files with semicolons between fields. Set the upload connection for this feed to auto-detect the delimiter. That day's file and the two rejected days imported with all nine columns.

tickets.classification_rationale: The amounts looked wrong, but they were mis-parsed while the file was being ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Belgian stores' revenue imported a hundred times too high
tickets.description: After each weekly file drop, sales for the customer's Belgian stores look one hundred times larger than reality. Files from other countries import correctly.
tickets.resolution_notes: The Belgian team's spreadsheet tool writes decimal commas, and the importer stripped the comma as a thousands separator, turning 1234,50 into 123450. Configured that team's feed for comma decimals and semicolon separators and reprocessed the last eight weekly files. Belgian revenue now matches the stores' till reports.

tickets.subject: SFTP files moved to 'rejected': header row not recognized
tickets.description: Files the merchandising team drops on the SFTP folder are being moved to the 'rejected' subfolder with 'Header row not recognized'.
tickets.resolution_notes: A team member had opened and re-saved the shared template on a laptop with German regional settings, which switched the separator to semicolons and turned the header into a single field. Enabled delimiter detection for this feed and asked the team to keep the template unchanged on the shared drive. The rejected files were reprocessed and the next three daily drops imported normally.

tickets.subject: SFTP inventory files ignored after server move
tickets.description: The customer's IT team moved the inventory export to a new server, and nothing from the SFTP folder has been imported since. There are no errors; the files just sit there.
tickets.resolution_notes: The new server names files 'inventory-2026-07-01.csv' instead of 'inventory_20260701.csv', which didn't match the connection's file pattern, so they were never picked up. Updated the pattern to accept both formats and imported the nine waiting files. The next morning's file was picked up within the 15-minute polling window.

tickets.subject: Store-traffic feed sometimes imports only part of a file
tickets.description: On some days the store-traffic feed imports only a fraction of the rows. Re-uploading the same file the next day always imports it completely.
tickets.resolution_notes: Large files were still being written to the SFTP folder when the connection polled, so it read a partial file and marked it processed. The connection now waits until a file's size is stable across two checks, and we suggested the customer upload under a temporary name and rename on completion. Every daily file over the following two weeks imported in full.

tickets.classification_rationale: This is the source CRM's allowance applied to our inbound connector, not our public API's rate limit, so sync rather than api.
tickets.subject: CRM sync stops mid-afternoon with 'request limit exceeded'
tickets.description: The customer's CRM sync fails most afternoons with 'REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED', and dashboards only have data up to the morning run.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's CRM enforces a daily API allowance shared by all connected apps, and a newly installed marketing tool was using most of it. Moved our sync to the CRM's bulk interface, which needs far fewer calls, and the customer capped the marketing tool's usage. Afternoon syncs have completed every day since.

tickets.subject: Month-end opportunity updates partly missing
tickets.description: At every month-end the pipeline dashboard lacks the last day's opportunity updates. The connector log shows the run stopping early with a quota message.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's month-end reporting tools used up the CRM's shared daily API allowance, and the connector stopped when it ran out. Scheduled our sync ahead of the reporting jobs and enabled resuming from the last checkpoint once the allowance resets. The following month-end synced completely.

tickets.classification_rationale: The lag looks like a performance issue, but it came from source-side throttling of ingestion, so sync rather than perf.
tickets.subject: Order data hours behind during weekend promotion
tickets.description: During a big weekend promotion, order data in the dashboard lagged three to four hours behind the storefront.
tickets.resolution_notes: The e-commerce platform throttled our connector to its standard request rate, and promotion volume exceeded what could be fetched at that rate. Switched the connection to the platform's order events so new orders arrive as they happen, with the scheduled sync kept as a catch-up. During the next promotion order data lagged by less than five minutes.

tickets.classification_rationale: The 429 responses come from the source POS platform during ingestion, not from our public API, so sync rather than api.
tickets.subject: Backfill keeps restarting after 429 responses from POS
tickets.description: While backfilling a year of transactions for a newly connected store group, the connector log fills with 429 'Too many requests' responses and the backfill starts over from the beginning.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector retried throttled requests immediately and, after repeated failures, restarted the whole backfill instead of resuming. Added exponential backoff that honours the platform's Retry-After header, plus a checkpoint every 1,000 transactions. The backfill finished in about six hours with all 1.4 million transactions.

tickets.subject: Loyalty sync succeeds only every other night
tickets.description: Loyalty transactions only update every second day. On the alternate nights the connector log shows 'Daily request allowance exhausted' within minutes of starting.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer's loyalty platform plan allows 50,000 API calls in a rolling 24 hours, and our connector re-read the entire member list nightly, using about 70,000 calls, so each run left too little allowance for the next. Changed the connector to fetch only members changed since the last run, which needs about 6,000 calls. Runs have completed every night for the following two weeks.

tickets.classification_rationale: Revenue looked wrong, but the status changes were never ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Cancelled orders still counted as sales
tickets.description: Orders cancelled in the e-commerce admin keep appearing as completed sales in the dashboard.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector only requested orders with status 'open' or 'fulfilled', so a change to 'cancelled' was never fetched. Added cancelled orders to the sync filter and re-synced the last 90 days. The 186 cancelled orders now show as cancelled and drop out of revenue.

tickets.subject: Accounts deleted in CRM months ago still listed
tickets.description: Accounts the customer deleted from their CRM during a cleanup months ago still appear in the account list and pipeline totals.
tickets.resolution_notes: Incremental sync only sees records that still exist, so hard-deleted records were never removed on our side. Enabled the CRM's deleted-records endpoint for this connection and ran a reconciliation that removed 741 accounts. Account totals now match the CRM.

tickets.subject: Till refunds missing from net sales
tickets.description: Net sales for one store look too high. The store manager says refunds processed at the till without the original receipt never show up.
tickets.resolution_notes: Receipt-less refunds are stored as standalone refund transactions in the POS, which the connector did not request. Added standalone refunds to the connector and backfilled them. The store's net sales now match the POS end-of-day reports for the past month.

tickets.subject: Archived products still show stock
tickets.description: Products archived in the e-commerce admin last season still have stock levels in the inventory dashboard.
tickets.resolution_notes: Archived products are left out of the platform's default product listing, so the connector stopped seeing them and kept their last stock values. The connector now requests archived products and marks them inactive with zero sellable stock. After the next sync 320 archived products dropped out of the inventory dashboard.

tickets.subject: Edits to shipped orders not reflected
tickets.description: When staff edit a shipped order to remove a damaged item and refund it, the dashboard keeps showing the original basket and total.
tickets.resolution_notes: The platform stores post-fulfilment edits as separate adjustment records linked to the order, and the connector only read the original order record. Added adjustment records to the order sync and applied them to the last 60 days. Edited orders now show their final baskets and totals.

tickets.classification_rationale: Notification emails are involved, but the issue is a paused ingestion schedule, so sync rather than alerts.
tickets.subject: Sync silently paused for two weeks
tickets.description: The customer only noticed stale data when a regional director asked why last week's numbers looked flat. The connector page reads 'Paused after 5 consecutive failures'.
tickets.resolution_notes: A brief source outage caused five failed runs and the connection paused itself; the failure emails went to an admin who had left the company. Resumed the schedule and backfilled the two weeks, and the admin changed the notification recipient to a shared operations address. Data is current, and a test failure notice reached the shared address.

tickets.subject: Weekly store KPIs frozen; connector paused with no warning
tickets.description: Weekly store KPIs stopped updating and the customer's analytics lead received no warning at all. The status page reads 'Paused – too many errors'.
tickets.resolution_notes: A series of expired-credential failures auto-paused the connection, and the only notification recipient was a deactivated user, so the warnings went unseen. Re-authorized, resumed and backfilled the connection, and notifications now also go to all workspace admins whenever the listed recipient is inactive. KPIs updated the next morning.

tickets.classification_rationale: Time zones are involved, but it is the sync schedule's run time rather than workspace preferences or data bucketing, so sync.
tickets.subject: Nightly POS sync runs before stores close
tickets.description: The nightly POS sync is supposed to run after closing, but the history shows it starting at 20:00 store time, so the last two hours of trading are missing until the following night.
tickets.resolution_notes: The 02:00 schedule was saved while the admin's profile time zone was UTC, and the stores are six hours behind UTC, so the run started at 20:00 local time. Set the schedule's time zone explicitly to the stores' zone. The next run started at 02:00 local time and included the full day's sales.

tickets.classification_rationale: A plan change triggered it, but no charge was wrong; the problem is sync frequency, so sync rather than billing.
tickets.subject: Hourly sync option greyed out after plan change
tickets.description: After the customer changed plans, their e-commerce connection dropped from hourly to daily syncs without anyone touching it, and the hourly option is now greyed out.
tickets.resolution_notes: The plan change re-applied connector defaults, and the workspace's entitlement for hourly syncs had not been refreshed for the new plan. Refreshed the entitlements and restored the hourly schedule. Hourly runs resumed the same afternoon.

tickets.subject: No sync on the night the clocks went forward
tickets.description: No sync ran on the night daylight-saving time began, so the next day's dashboards showed the previous day's data until the following night.
tickets.resolution_notes: The schedule was set for 02:30 local time, which did not exist that night, and the scheduler skipped the non-existent time instead of running at the next valid one. Ran a manual catch-up sync and changed the scheduler to run skipped times immediately afterwards. A simulated run against the next transition date started at 03:00 as expected.

tickets.classification_rationale: Access rights are involved, but they are the connector's permissions in the source CRM, not user roles in our app, so sync rather than perm.
tickets.subject: No opportunities for the APAC region
tickets.description: The pipeline dashboard shows no APAC opportunities at all, although the CRM has hundreds. Every other region looks complete.
tickets.resolution_notes: The integration user in the customer's CRM had a role that only saw records shared within its own region hierarchy, which excluded APAC. The CRM admin granted the integration user read access to all regions. A full resync brought in 642 APAC opportunities.

tickets.classification_rationale: Values were blank, but they were never ingested because of a missing connector scope, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Discount codes blank on every synced order
tickets.description: Every synced order shows an empty discount code, including orders the customer knows used promo codes.
tickets.resolution_notes: The app installation in the customer's e-commerce admin had never been granted the 'read discounts' scope, so discount details were left out of order data. The store owner approved the additional scope from the connector settings. Re-syncing the last 30 days filled in discount codes on 3,940 orders.

tickets.classification_rationale: The margin widgets looked broken, but cost values never reached us because of field permissions in the source, so sync rather than render or perm.
tickets.subject: Product cost empty for every item from ERP
tickets.description: Margin widgets have no data because product cost is empty for every item, even though the merchandising team can see costs in the ERP.
tickets.resolution_notes: Field-level security in the ERP hid the unit cost field from the integration account, so the API returned it empty. The customer's ERP admin granted that account read access to the field. After a resync, unit costs populated for all 8,200 products and the margin widgets displayed.

tickets.subject: Quote dashboard empty; sync warns about object access
tickets.description: The quote conversion dashboard is empty. Each CRM sync completes 'with warnings', and the details read 'Insufficient access rights on object Quote'.
tickets.resolution_notes: During a security review the customer had moved the integration user to a restricted profile that no longer included read access to quotes. Their CRM admin restored read-only access to quote objects for that user. The next sync imported 2,215 quotes and the dashboard populated.

tickets.subject: Only the reconnecting rep's own accounts sync
tickets.description: After the customer reconnected the CRM integration, only accounts owned by the person who reconnected it are imported, about 5% of the usual volume.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connection had been re-authorized with a sales rep's personal login, whose CRM visibility is limited to their own records. Re-authorized with the dedicated integration user, which can read all accounts. Account volume returned to the usual 23,000 on the next run.

tickets.subject: Newly opened outlet's sales missing everywhere
tickets.description: A new outlet opened two weeks ago and its sales are missing from every dashboard. The e-commerce connector lists only the original locations.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connector syncs the locations selected at setup and did not add new ones automatically. Selected the new location, enabled 'Include new locations automatically', and backfilled from the opening date. The outlet's two weeks of sales now appear.

tickets.subject: Sales dashboard full of 'TEST ITEM' orders
tickets.description: The customer sees orders for products such as 'TEST ITEM DO NOT SHIP' in the sales dashboard, and their real sales are nowhere to be found.
tickets.resolution_notes: During setup the connector had been authorized against the customer's sandbox store instead of the production store. Reconnected to production, removed the sandbox data and backfilled 12 months of real orders. The sales dashboard now shows only production orders.

tickets.subject: UK storefront absent from global sales dashboard
tickets.description: The global sales dashboard includes the US and Canadian storefronts but nothing from the UK site, which launched under the same organization account in the spring.
tickets.resolution_notes: Each storefront is a separate shop on the platform, and the organization-level connection only covered shops that existed when it was authorized. Re-authorized at organization level to include the UK shop and backfilled from its launch date. UK orders now appear and the global total matches the platform's organization report.

tickets.subject: Ad spend from the outlet brand's account missing
tickets.description: The marketing ROI dashboard shows spend only for the main brand. Spend for the outlet brand, which runs from a separate advertising account, is missing.
tickets.resolution_notes: The advertising connector was set up with the default account only, and the outlet brand's account was added to the customer's manager account later. Added the second account to the connection and backfilled 180 days. Combined spend now matches the totals in the advertising platform.

tickets.subject: Connector still reading the retired CRM instance
tickets.description: Pipeline numbers stopped changing a month ago. The customer migrated to a new CRM instance in April, yet our connector keeps reporting successful runs.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connection still pointed at the old instance, which became read-only after the migration, so runs succeeded but found no changes. Connected the new instance, mapped old record IDs to new ones using the migration's ID mapping file, and backfilled. Pipeline numbers now track the new instance with history preserved.

tickets.subject: Initial load stopped at 18 months of history
tickets.description: Customer connected their POS expecting five years of history, but transactions only go back 18 months.
tickets.resolution_notes: The connection was created with the default 18-month backfill start date, and the setup screen did not make that obvious. Extended the start date to five years and ran the historical load in yearly chunks. All five years loaded over two nights, and the year-over-year charts now include prior years.

tickets.classification_rationale: A timeout is involved, but it is a one-off ingestion run hitting its duration cap rather than slowness in the app, so sync rather than perf.
tickets.subject: First full sync fails after exactly six hours
tickets.description: The first full sync of a large grocery chain's e-commerce data fails after six hours every time with 'Run exceeded maximum duration'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The initial load tried to import eight years of orders in a single run, hit the six-hour limit and discarded its progress. Split the backfill into monthly segments that run back to back and keep their progress. The backfill finished in 31 hours across segments with 9.6 million orders.

tickets.subject: Retrying the initial load doubled January
tickets.description: During onboarding the customer clicked 'Retry' after the historical load hit an error. The first month of history now shows double sales.
tickets.resolution_notes: Retrying a failed backfill restarted it from the start date without removing the rows already loaded for the first segment. Removed the duplicate segment and changed retries to resume from the last completed segment. January totals now match the source, and a test retry resumed correctly.

tickets.classification_rationale: Looks like a mapping error, but the related customer records were never ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.
tickets.subject: Older orders show 'Unknown customer' after onboarding
tickets.description: Five years of orders loaded during onboarding, but every order older than two years shows 'Unknown customer'.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer backfill kept the default 24-month window while the order backfill used five years, so older orders referenced customers that were never imported. Aligned the customer backfill with the orders and reloaded customers back to the earliest order. 'Unknown customer' rows dropped from 41,000 to zero.

tickets.classification_rationale: A queue is involved, but the delay is ingestion ordering for one connection rather than overall application load, so sync rather than perf.
tickets.subject: Historical load blocks yesterday's sales from arriving
tickets.description: A newly connected store group's historical load is still running on day three, and yesterday's sales aren't appearing because the daily sync is queued behind it.
tickets.resolution_notes: Backfill and incremental syncs shared one queue per connection, so the long historical load blocked daily updates. Enabled incremental sync to run alongside a backfill, writing recent data first. Yesterday's sales appeared within the hour, and the backfill finished the next day.

tickets.subject: Returns history starts on the day the connector was installed
tickets.description: The returns-rate dashboard only has returns from the date the connector was installed; every earlier month shows zero returns.
tickets.resolution_notes: The backfill job covered orders but not returns, because returns were added to the connector after the job's object list was fixed. Added returns to the backfill configuration for all connections and reloaded this customer's return history. Returns now appear back to the start of the order history.

tickets.classification_rationale: Webhooks are involved, but these are inbound events from the source used to ingest data, so sync rather than api (our outbound webhooks).
tickets.subject: Live order ticker now updates only overnight
tickets.description: The live sales ticker used to update within a minute of each online order. Since Wednesday, new orders only appear after the nightly sync.
tickets.resolution_notes: The customer rotated the webhook signing secret in their e-commerce admin, and our connector still verified events against the old secret, so it rejected every one. Updated the secret in the connector settings. Live orders began appearing within a minute again and the rejected-events counter returned to zero.

tickets.subject: Inbound events discarded with 'signature mismatch'
tickets.description: The event log for the Northwind Commerce connection shows hundreds of 'Signature mismatch – event discarded' entries an hour. The dashboard only catches up after each scheduled sync.
tickets.resolution_notes: During a security review the store owner regenerated the shared secret used to sign events, while the connector still held the previous value. Entered the new secret and replayed the discarded events from the platform's event history. Event ingestion resumed with no further mismatches.

tickets.subject: Stock levels lag a day after quarterly key rotation
tickets.description: Inventory on the store dashboard now trails reality by about a day. The customer's IT team mentions rotating integration keys in their commerce platform last week under a quarterly policy.
tickets.resolution_notes: The rotation included the event signing secret, so the connector rejected every inventory event and only the daily scheduled sync delivered changes. Updated the secret and added a connector-page warning when more than 5% of events fail verification within an hour. Inventory changes now arrive within two minutes.

tickets.subject: Real-time orders stopped after app reinstall
tickets.description: After the store owner reinstalled our app in their e-commerce admin, the live order feed went quiet. Scheduled syncs still work.
tickets.resolution_notes: Reinstalling the app removed its event subscriptions in the store, and the install flow did not recreate them. Recreated the order and inventory subscriptions and changed the install flow to register them automatically. Live orders resumed immediately, and the subscriptions survived a test reinstall.

tickets.classification_rationale: High load is involved, but the result was lost ingestion of source events, so sync rather than perf.
tickets.subject: Live dashboard missed orders during flash sale
tickets.description: During a two-hour flash sale, the live dashboard missed about 8% of orders until the nightly sync filled the gap.
tickets.resolution_notes: Our event intake endpoint returned errors when its processing queue was full, and the platform gave up on those events after three attempts. Increased intake capacity and changed the endpoint to accept and queue events before processing them. During the next flash sale every order appeared on the live dashboard.

tickets.subject: Second online store never appears in real time
tickets.description: The customer connected a second online store to the same workspace. Its orders appear after the nightly sync but never live.
tickets.resolution_notes: The second store was added through 'Add shop' on the existing connection, which skipped event registration, so subscriptions existed only for the first store. Registered subscriptions for the second store and fixed 'Add shop' to register them too. Orders from both stores now reach the live feed within a minute.
